title: When the Microsoft 365 connector hits an error, how much of the error text may it hand back to the admin's browser?
bluf: Secuura/Blockchain, the Microsoft 365 connector service. Three places still pass error text we do not control back to a signed-in admin: the sign-in redirect after a failed token exchange (KS-1641, the line the ticket calls ':515'), a 500 reply to a failed token refresh that includes the raw internal error (KS-1670 site 2), and OneDrive replies that pass Microsoft's own error text back unchanged (KS-1670 site 3). I read all three in the code (local copy of develop at 1b1b65c7415f, which is behind GitHub's develop; not re-read at the newest commit): the refresh reply is at index.ts line 874, the OneDrive reply at line 1173, the redirect at line 689. All three need a valid session or server-issued id, so none is open to an anonymous caller. Measured: nothing live; unmeasured: whether the admin screens show that text to a person (it decides what we lose by hiding it). Our own earlier fixes (KS-1410) already replaced internal error text with the fixed sentence 'An unexpected error occurred' and logged the real one, so I recommend that for the two internal errors and a 200-character cap for Microsoft's own text.

options.label: Fixed sentence or short code everywhere, real error only in the server log
options.detail: Safest and one rule for all three; an admin loses Microsoft's own explanation when OneDrive refuses, and support must read logs.

options.label: Fixed sentence for our own internal errors (refresh 500 and the redirect), 200-character cap for Microsoft's text
options.detail: Matches what KS-1410 already shipped for internal text; the OneDrive reply stays useful to the admin; the ticket says the sign-in service caps provider text at 200 (I did not re-read that code).

options.label: Leave all three as they are
options.detail: No work; the admin keeps seeing raw error text; the sites stay listed as open.

default_action: Option c for sites 2 and 3: nothing is built and both tickets stay open. Site 1 of KS-1670 is already merged and deployed to Kintsugi. KS-1744 (the redirect rule Peter wrote, assigned to Kam's account) proceeds on its own written scope. Wednesday asks no agent to build until you tap.

title: Should the MCP server's web interface stop hashing any file on the server that a caller names, and stop echoing error text?
bluf: Secuura/Blockchain, the MCP server's web interface (mcp-server http-server.ts). Four routes (hash, register-batch, verify, verify-batch) will read any file path the caller sends, check no password or key, and hash it; error replies also say whether a path exists. KS-1410 (error text) fixed the other nine 500 replies in that file and deliberately left POST /hash and the per-item errors in batch replies; KS-1214 is the same route seen as an access problem. I read the code (local copy of develop at 1b1b65c7415f, behind GitHub's tip): all four routes call the file hasher with the caller's path. By the repo's own settings the port is reachable only inside the container network and the gateway forwards only one MCP route. Whether the deployed machines expose it is UNMEASURED (the closing read is a read-only look at Kintsugi; the demo is frozen and stays untouched). Counter-point read in the published OpenAPI: it describes filePath as 'for local execution', so removing it could break a documented use; whether any client sends it is unmeasured. These are one decision, so one card: I recommend measuring the exposure read-only and building the removal and the fixed error text now with no deploy.

options.label: Remove file-path reading from the web interface; fixed error sentence on /hash and batch items
options.detail: Closes the hole whatever the exposure is; breaks any client that sends a server path (none known, none checked).

options.label: Keep file-path reading but require the API key the spec already declares
options.detail: Keeps the 'local execution' use; needs an auth design decision and a build on a security surface (tier 1).

options.label: Measure exposure first (read-only look at Kintsugi) and decide after
options.detail: Costs a day; nothing changes meanwhile. Does not cover the error-text half.

options.label: Leave as is, internal-only by configuration
options.detail: No work; the package generator text (per the ticket) tells users to expose the server publicly, so that rests on configuration alone.

default_action: Option c's read-only half: Seat U asks for a read-only Kintsugi exposure measurement and nothing is built or changed. KS-1410 and KS-1214 stay open. Wednesday builds nothing until you tap.

title: If the anchoring service has no Cardano connection set up, should it count that as the chain saying 'not found'?
bluf: Secuura/Blockchain, anchoring service, a fee-paying money path. Your earlier ruling on KS-1171 (card secuura-ks1171-when-is-an-anchor-absent = c: absent only after 2 answered polls and an answer at least 60 s after the node's 400) is built, merged and in the Kintsugi code by the ticket's own comments. This card is only the one item that ruling did not cover, '8k': when no Blockfrost connection is configured, getTransaction returns 'not found' (provider.ts line 452, read in the local copy of develop at 1b1b65c7415f, behind GitHub's tip), and the poll counter treats that as the chain answering. The ticket calls it unreachable in production without a real 64-character hash on the row; I did not measure that. Three code paths call getTransaction (confirmation.ts, cardano/index.ts, index.ts); I read the use in confirmation.ts and the four lines around the one in index.ts, not the one in cardano/index.ts. The code comment says an unconfigured service falls back to 'mock mode', so whether the change affects mock-mode flows is UNMEASURED. I recommend the narrow fix: treat 'no connection' as unknown inside the re-poll only, consistent with your strictest-rule ruling.

options.label: Make an unconfigured connection an error everywhere (getTransaction throws)
options.detail: Cleanest meaning; reaches all three callers, two of which I did not fully read.

options.label: Narrow fix: only the re-poll treats 'no connection' as unknown, never as an answer
options.detail: Consistent with your 09-25 ruling; touches the re-poll only; tier 1 gate; no deploy without your word.

options.label: Leave it and close 8k as won't-fix, recorded as unreachable in production
options.detail: No money-path change; rests on the ticket's claim, which is not measured.

default_action: Option c's no-build half: 8k is left open and listed; no agent changes anything on this money path. Wednesday does not close the ticket. KS-1171 stays In Progress.
